zoe: Pushed a small docs PR to clarify Dedicated provisioning examples and add a short note about cooldown tradeoffs. URL: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4721
docs-bot: [linkcheck] scanning PR #4721 for broken links and anchors
ellen: Thanks Zoe. Quick scan: the HCL module source points at an internal repo path; we should switch to the public terraform module path or note that it's internal-only.
paul: also, the new section "Why cooldown matters" is good but could use one practical sentence connecting cooldown to KV cache hit-rate and cold-start cost spikes.
zoe: good point, Paul. I'll add a sentence and a tiny graph suggestion. Can someone sanity-check the Python SDK snippet for provisioning? I tried to keep it minimal and async.

zoe: ```python
# minimal async provisioning with py SDK
import asyncio
from redwood import DedicatedAsyncClient

async def main():
    client = DedicatedAsyncClient(org='acme')
    cfg = {
        'pool': 'us-east-1-dedicated',
        'autoscale': {
            'min': 1,
            'max': 10,
            'cooldown_seconds': 450,
            'metric': 'latency_p95'
        }
    }
    resp = await client.create_capacity(cfg)
    print('request id:', resp['request_id'])

asyncio.run(main())
```
docs-bot: [auto-edit] PR branch: adjusted code fence language to "python" and changed one markdown heading for consistency

kai: The SDK example uses keys like 'min'/'max' vs the rest of the docs which use 'min_replicas'/'max_replicas'. We should be consistent. I'd lean toward explicit names (min_replicas).
paul: +1 on explicit names. Also, consider a short callout: "short cooldowns can cause rapid replica churn across tenants when request bursts are correlated" under "Isolation considerations." That helps product teams who wonder about noisy neighbors.
ellen: SLA wording question: the doc currently says "SLA: < 100ms median" — legal wants us to avoid promises in docs. Suggest rephrase to "target median latency" and link to the formal SLA page for contract terms.
zoe: I'll update wording to "target median latency" and add the link to the SLA page. Which link should I use? infra-bot: Suggested link: https://console.redwood.ai/sla (internal).

zoe: Updated the PR: switched HCL module source to the public module path and normalized the YAML/JSON keys to use min_replicas/max_replicas. Also added a one-paragraph explainer tying cooldowns to cache warmup and replica churn.

paul: tiny nit on HCL example - add a comments block showing how to set tenant labels so people see the isolation knob.

zoe: added HCL comment and a short example:```hcl
module "dedicated_pool" {
  source = "github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules//dedicated"
  pool_name = "us-east-1-dedicated"
  min_replicas = 1
  max_replicas = 10
  cooldown_seconds = 450
  # tenant_labels allow routing/affinity per-tenant
  # tenant_labels = { team = "analytics" }
}
```

kai: LGTM after the key-name alignment and the SLA phrasing change. I can give final signoff in ~15m.
docs-bot: [CI] lint & linkcheck passed for PR #4721

zoe: thanks all — merging after Kai's signoff. Quick release note I'll add: "docs: clarify cooldown rationale, standardize provisioning keys, add async python + HCL examples, update SLA phrasing". If anything weird shows up, tag #eng-oncall. :thumbsup:
